prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production sprite sheet for a NEW post-corgi worker in The Daily Meili, matching the supplied Pip sprite as style reference, not the same character. Transparent background. Chunky crisp pixel art, tiny readable black-dot eyes, warm orange-and-white slim Pembroke corgi, black tiny eyebrows. Charcoal outlines, restrained flat sage postal cap between visible ears, small burgundy neckerchief and sage crossbody mail satchel. No glasses. Cute dignified little postal dog, NOT bipedal. Exactly four legs with connected anatomy in walking frames, short dog body. No props in his mouth. All poses fully visible with generous empty gutters, same pixel scale.
Single 3-column by 2-row atlas (six equal 512x512 cells in 1536x1024 layout), NO grid lines or text.
Top row: 1) seated idle in three-quarter view facing screen-right; 2) seated in SAME position with chin tipped up looking attentively at a chute above-right, eyes looking up, ears perked; 3) same seated up-looking pose, tiny tail-wag variation. Bottom row: three consecutive four-legged WALK RIGHT frames of that SAME postal corgi, consistent head/body/satchel and ground line, subtly alternate paws. Clear silhouettes and consistent proportions across all six. Match Pip's chunky pixels and simple face; no painterly gradients or fuzz, no scenery, no lettering, no shadows outside the sprite. Keep background truly transparent.
